verdict_reason: Roles replacement and the roles-required, unknown-role and receiving-role-outside-UK refusals on PUT are covered and can fail, but three new titles over-claim 'stored values' and the stale-version test is titled as a PUT behaviour it does not exercise.

todos.issue: Three added tests claim 'KeepStoredValues' — put_shouldReturn400KeyedByRolesAndKeepStoredValues_whenBodyOmitsRoles (:87), ..._whenARoleIsUnknown (:100), put_shouldReturn400KeyedByCountryCodeAndKeepStoredValues_whenAReceivingRoleIsOutsideTheUk (:113) — but each asserts only assertStoredRolesAreStillTheSeededOnes (:38), the stored roles. The seeded addressLine2 'Unit 3' and county 'Highland', which a wrongly accepted PUT of addressBody() would clear, are never checked.
todos.fix: Must: each title states what its assertions prove. One way: rename to ...AndKeepStoredRoles..., or have the helper assert the whole stored address (roles, addressLine2, county, countryCode) is unchanged.

todos.issue: put_shouldRejectStaleVersion_whenRowWasUpdatedConcurrently (:201) titles the PUT as the thing that rejects, but the PUT in it succeeds (isOk) and the assertion is that a direct addressRepository.save(stale) throws OptimisticLockingFailureException: it proves the entity's @Version check, not anything the PUT endpoint rejects. The endpoint-level refusal is put_shouldReturn409ConflictProblem_whenOptimisticLockingFails (:187).
todos.fix: Must: the title names what the assertion proves. One way: rename to save_shouldThrowOptimisticLockingFailure_whenTheAddressWasUpdatedSinceItWasRead, or move it to AddressRepositoryIT beside the other repository-level tests.
